title: CodeRabbit raised $143m to read the code AI wrote
excerpt: The CodeRabbit Series C raised $143m at a $1.5bn valuation, co-led by Atomico, to review the code AI agents now write faster than humans read.
content_html:
Code review is the step where somebody reads a change before it ships. A developer proposes an edit, opens what the trade calls a pull request, and a colleague checks it for bugs and security holes.

It is slow and unglamorous work. Until recently it was also manageable, because roughly one human wrote each change and roughly one human read it.

That ratio has broken. Coding agents now work for hours at a stretch and open pull requests with barely any human involvement.

On Wednesday CodeRabbit said it had raised $143m to sit in the gap. Bloomberg reported the round before the announcement. Atomico and Smash Capital co-led it.

Chief executive Harjot Gill gave the post-money figure to Axios Pro as $1.5bn. He and Gur Singh founded the company in San Francisco in 2023. Gill had sold an earlier startup, Netsil, to Nutanix in 2018.

Nobody is reading what the agents write

The company sources the problem from outside itself. GitHub is on pace to record 14 times more commits this year, on its chief operating officer’s own figures. Among firms in the top decile of coding-agent adoption, agents open 35% of pull requests, according to Jellyfish.

Demand for the agents keeps outrunning supply. GitHub Copilot paused new signups rather than let usage run away from it.

“AI made code plentiful,” CodeRabbit wrote on X. “Trust is now the bottleneck.”

The product reviews changes automatically. It flags bugs, security flaws and maintainability risks, and it explains what each change does. It runs more than two million reviews a week for over 17,000 customers, the company said in its funding release. Nvidia, BMW, Adyen, Indeed, JFrog and Trivago are among them.

A European fund co-led an American round

Atomico is a London firm, and it does not often co-lead US growth rounds of this size. Partner Luca Eisenstecken takes a board seat.

“As AI becomes critical infrastructure for the global economy, organisations will increasingly need independent governance layers that can validate software regardless of which model produced it,” Eisenstecken said.

The money follows the customers. CodeRabbit has opened an office in Moorgate in London and now employs 50 people across the UK and the EU. It plans to double that European headcount, then move into Japan and Singapore.

BMW i Ventures also joined the round. Managing partner Kasper Sage said carmakers depend on reliable software and efficient engineering teams. BMW is already a CodeRabbit customer, so the fund is backing a product its own engineers use.

Several backers sit on both sides of the ledger. Datadog is a new investor. Nvidia was already one, and it is a customer as well.

That Nvidia tie is technical, not only financial. CodeRabbit post-trained Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning model to handle one of its highest-volume routing jobs. Existing backers CRV, Scale Venture Partners, Flex Capital and Pelion Venture Partners all returned.

The bigger claim is that Jira is finished

CodeRabbit announced a product category alongside the money, and called it Agentic Change Management. The founders’ blog post puts it more bluntly. “Issue tracking is dead.”

The argument runs like this. Trackers such as Jira were built when writing code was expensive, so teams planned first and built second. AI reverses that order. Code now exists before anyone has decided whether it is worth having.

Anyone can start a change, too. OpenAI has pushed Codex at non-developers for much the same reason.

Three new tools follow from that. Triage scores incoming pull requests by value, urgency and risk, then routes the low-risk ones into automation. Change Stack groups a large agent-written diff into layers a human can follow. CodeRabbit Security scans code that has already shipped.

Security is what the cheque was really for

Large language models cut the cost of finding vulnerabilities. That helps defenders and attackers equally. It is why the security product arrived with the round rather than after it.

“Security now requires a continuous system that can reason across the repository, verify whether a threat is real, and move the fix back through the development workflow,” said Brad Twohig, founding partner at Smash Capital.

The desk has covered the failure mode before. Lovable’s vibe-coding platform ran into a security crisis of its own.

The supply chain shows the same shape. An npm worm spread through developer packages this year.

The market is smaller than the company

Here is the awkward number. The global code review services market is worth about $3.04bn this year and should reach $4.79bn by 2032, on 360iResearch figures cited by Tech Funding News.

CodeRabbit is valued at $1.5bn. That is roughly half the entire market it currently sells into.

The valuation only works if code review stops being a developer tool and becomes infrastructure. Gill says the pull is there. “It’s almost like a land grab moment for us,” he told Bloomberg.

Rivals are grabbing too. Qodo raised a $70m Series B led by Qumra Capital, Greptile raised a Series A at a $180m valuation, and CodeAnt AI closed a $2m seed.

Cost is the other pressure. Gartner expects AI coding to cost more than developers by 2028, and a review layer adds to that bill rather than trimming it.

What the company did not disclose

Revenue grew more than five times year over year, CodeRabbit said. It did not say what it grew from. The multiple therefore carries no absolute figure.

Total funding is about $231m by Tech Funding News arithmetic, counting a $16m Series A in 2024 and a $60m Series B last September. Bloomberg puts the total at more than $200m.

The company will also spend $10m over 12 months keeping the tool free for open-source maintainers, Reuters reported. That covers 150,000 projects.

What would settle it

Two things are checkable rather than rhetorical. The first is the London headcount, which the company says will double from 50.

The second is the real claim. “Issue tracking is dead” is a big sentence, and it stops being marketing on the day a named customer says it dropped Jira for CodeRabbit Triage.

Until then this is a very well funded company selling a fix for a problem the AI industry created, to the same industry that created it.

content_html_zh:
代码审查是有人在发布之前阅读更改的步骤。 开发人员提出编辑建议，打开业内所谓的拉取请求，同事检查其中是否存在错误和安全漏洞。

这是一项缓慢而乏味的工作。 直到最近，它还是可以管理的，因为每个更改大约有一个人编写，并且大约有一个人阅读它。

这个比例已经被打破了。 编码代理现在可以连续工作几个小时并打开拉取请求，几乎不需要任何人工参与。

周三，CodeRabbit 表示已筹集 1.43 亿美元来弥补这一缺口。 彭博社在宣布之前报道了本轮融资。 Atomico 和 Smash Capital 共同领导。

首席执行官 Harjot Gill 向 Axios Pro 透露的财务数字为 15 亿美元。 他和 Gur Singh 于 2023 年在旧金山创立了这家公司。 Gill 于 2018 年将一家早期初创公司 Netsil 出售给了 Nutanix。

没有人读特工写的东西

该公司将问题归咎于外部。 根据其首席运营官自己的数据，GitHub 今年的提交量有望增加 14 倍。 据 Jellyfish 称，在采用编码代理的前十分之一的公司中，代理打开了 35% 的拉取请求。

对代理商的需求一直供不应求。 GitHub Copilot 暂停了新的注册，而不是让使用量流失。

“人工智能让代码变得丰富，”CodeRabbit 在 X 上写道。 “信任现在是瓶颈。”

产品评论会自动更改。 它标记了错误、安全缺陷和可维护性风险，并解释了每个更改的作用。 该公司在融资新闻稿中表示，它每周为 17,000 多名客户提供超过 200 万条评论。 其中包括 Nvidia、BMW、Adyen、Indeed、JFrog 和 Trivago。

一家欧洲基金联合领投美国一轮融资

Atomico 是一家伦敦公司，它并不经常共同领导美国这种规模的增长轮融资。 合伙人 Luca Eisenstecken 获得董事会席位。

Eisenstecken 表示：“随着人工智能成为全球经济的关键基础设施，组织将越来越需要独立的治理层来验证软件，无论软件是哪种模型生成的。”

钱跟着顾客走。 CodeRabbit 在伦敦 Moorgate 开设了办事处，目前在英国和欧盟拥有 50 名员工。 该公司计划将欧洲员工人数增加一倍，然后进军日本和新加坡。

BMW i Ventures 也加入了此轮融资。 管理合伙人 Kasper Sage 表示，汽车制造商依赖可靠的软件和高效的工程团队。 宝马已经是 CodeRabbit 的客户，因此该基金正在支持其工程师使用的产品。

账本两侧都有几个支持者。 Datadog 是新投资者。 英伟达已经是其中之一，而且它也是客户。

与英伟达的关系是技术上的，而不仅仅是财务上的。 CodeRabbit 对 Nvidia 的 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 模型进行了后训练，以处理其容量最大的路由工作之一。 现有支持者 CRV、Scale Venture Partners、Flex Capital 和 Pelion Venture Partners 均回归。

更大的主张是 Jira 已经完成了

CodeRabbit 在提供资金的同时还宣布了一个产品类别，并将其称为 Agentic Change Management。 创始人的博客文章说得更直白。 “问题跟踪已死。”

论证是这样的。 像 Jira 这样的跟踪器是在编写代码成本昂贵的时候构建的，因此团队首先进行规划，然后进行构建。 人工智能颠倒了这个顺序。 现在，在任何人决定是否值得拥有代码之前，代码就已经存在了。

任何人都可以开始改变。 出于同样的原因，OpenAI 将 Codex 推向非开发人员。

随后出现了三个新工具。 分类根据价值、紧迫性和风险对传入的拉取请求进行评分，然后将低风险的请求路由到自动化。 更改堆栈将代理编写的大型差异分组为人类可以遵循的层。 CodeRabbit Security 扫描已发送的代码。

安全才是支票的真正目的

大型语言模型降低了发现漏洞的成本。 这对防守者和进攻者都有同样的帮助。 这就是为什么安全产品是随回合一起出现的，而不是在回合之后出现的。

Smash Capital 创始合伙人 Brad Twohig 表示：“安全性现在需要一个连续的系统，可以跨存储库进行推理，验证威胁是否真实，并将修复程序移回到开发工作流程中。”

桌子之前已经介绍过故障模式。 Lovable 的振动编码平台本身也遇到了安全危机。

供应链呈现出相同的形状。 今年，npm 蠕虫病毒通过开发者包传播。

市场比公司小

这是一个尴尬的数字。 Tech Funding News 援引 360iResearch 的数据显示，今年全球代码审查服务市场价值约为 30.4 亿美元，到 2032 年预计将达到 47.9 亿美元。

CodeRabbit 的估值为 15 亿美元。 这大约占其目前销售的整个市场的一半。

只有当代码审查不再是开发人员工具并成为基础设施时，评估才有效。 吉尔说，拉力就在那里。 “这对我们来说几乎就像是一个抢地的时刻，”他告诉彭博社。

竞争对手也在争夺。 Qodo 筹集了由 Qumra Capital 领投的 7000 万美元 B 轮融资，Greptile 筹集了估值 1.8 亿美元的 A 轮融资，CodeAnt AI 完成了 200 万美元种子轮融资。

成本是另一个压力。 Gartner 预计，到 2028 年，人工智能编码的成本将超过开发人员，而审查层会增加而不是削减该费用。

该公司未透露的内容

CodeRabbit 表示，收入同比增长五倍多。 它没有说它是从什么开始的。 因此，倍数没有绝对数字。

根据 Tech Funding News 计算，总融资额约为 2.31 亿美元，其中包括 2024 年 1600 万美元的 A 轮融资和去年 9 月的 6000 万美元 B 轮融资。 彭博社估计总金额超过 2 亿美元。

据路透社报道，该公司还将在 12 个月内花费 1000 万美元，为开源维护人员免费提供该工具。 这涵盖了 150,000 个项目。

什么可以解决它

有两件事是可以检查的，而不是说说而已。 首先是伦敦的员工人数，该公司称其数量将从 50 人增加一倍。

第二是真实的主张。 “问题跟踪已死”是一句大话，在一位指定客户表示放弃 Jira 转而使用 CodeRabbit Triage 的那天，它就停止了营销活动。

在那之前，这是一家资金雄厚的公司，向制造该问题的同一个行业出售人工智能行业所产生问题的解决方案。
